F_Fleet.name: Fleet / Crown stewardship
F_Fleet.description: Mature post-Shattering Fleet authority responsible for patrol, relief, survey support, corridor protection and the institutional guarantee behind much of the public transit network.
symbols: blue, gold and white Fleet colors
F_Fleet.politicalNotes: The Fleet is not symbolically green because it is not the civilian population that depends on the road. Blue and gold express authority and stewardship: the institution that surveys, maintains, certifies and protects the King's-Road-like network on which others build their lives.

F_BHA.name: Beacon Harmonics Authority
F_BHA.description: Present-day technical authority that monitors beacon harmonics, local inverse-tension conditions, sensor health and public corridor certification.
F_BHA.politicalNotes: Green is a measured public condition, not BHA ownership. Red can mean dangerous field conditions or failed/insufficient sensing. Internal diagnostics and unpublished harmonic data can become highly valuable if leaked.

F_Verge.name: The Verge
F_Verge.description: Ordinary frontier communities, farms, markets, ports, families, traders and local governments whose daily continuity depends on reliable public corridors.
F_Verge.politicalNotes: Green belongs culturally to the people who rely on safe connection. A route turning red is not abstract infrastructure news to the Verge; it can mean food, medicine, family and markets stop moving.

F_Shards.name: The Shards / Confederacy
F_Shards.description: Post-Shattering settlements, captains, salvagers, survival blocs and armed formations strongest where public corridor authority is weak or absent.
F_Shards.politicalNotes: Bright red expresses fracture from the green public network. Shard power can grow around red, unmarked or independently held routes, and hostile actors can sometimes benefit simply by making a public route too uncertain to certify.

F_PrivateSurvey.name: Independent Survey Culture
F_PrivateSurvey.description: Private survey ships and crews that measure reciprocal-field geometry outside or beyond the certified public network and sell route knowledge commercially.
symbols: purple hull fields and survey markings
F_PrivateSurvey.politicalNotes: Private surveyors serve legitimate freight, isolated settlements, explorers, blockade runners, smugglers and others. A private route may be unmarked or privately marked; neither condition makes it BHA-certified.

F_Trade.name: Route Brokers / Veil Market
F_Trade.description: Middlemen who buy, combine, repackage and resell route observations, timing windows, sensor information and access.
F_Trade.politicalNotes: Some brokers provide useful liquidity and anonymization; others strip provenance, age or limitations from survey data because ambiguity is profitable. The same route package may reach legitimate and illegitimate buyers.

F_Tempest.name: Tempest formations
F_Tempest.description: Fleet martial and patrol formations designed to operate at the margins of corridor protection and beyond ordinary green-route assumptions.
F_Tempest.politicalNotes: Tempest represents the warring/protective side of Fleet stewardship: the Crown moving beyond the King's Road to protect the places where the road itself is not enough.

F_Crimson.name: Crimson formations
F_Crimson.description: Heavy Fleet protection formations with a harder security orientation but full present-era alignment with Fleet command.
F_Crimson.politicalNotes: Crimson is not bright Shard red. In the current known era these crews are friendly and aligned, with aggressive posture explained by their protective mission. Do not villain-code them or foreshadow later internal conflict as secret present-day betrayal.

F_BlockadeRunner.name: Blockade-runner tradition
F_BlockadeRunner.description: Highly attuned fast-transit ships and crews that preserve an intensified version of the proto-Fleet navigation ethos.
F_BlockadeRunner.politicalNotes: Cyan is a sharpened echo of Fleet blue rather than a rebellion color. Their identity comes from extreme navigation competence and the willingness to operate where normal public-route assumptions are insufficient.
